recipes.name: Christmas Cornflake Wreath Cookies
ingredients_raw: 1 teaspoon green food coloring, or as needed
1 (2.25 ounce) package cinnamon red hot candies

steps.text: Line a baking tray with waxed paper.
Place marshmallows and butter in a microwave-safe bowl; microwave on high for 2 minutes. Stir, then microwave on high for 2 minutes more; stir.
Mix in coloring, almond extract, and vanilla until the desired color is reached; gently stir in cornflakes to coat.
Drop by tablespoonfuls onto the prepared tray and use lightly greased fingers to form wreath shapes; decorate with 3 red hots each.
Allow cookies to cool and set, about 15 minutes; store in an airtight container.

raw_recipe.headline: Christmas Cornflake Wreath Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These colorful cornflake wreaths are super easy to make and fun to eat! Perfect for parties and for kids to get creative during the holidays.

review.reviewBody: This recipe is very similar to one I grew up with but we call them Holly Cookies -- we just don't add the extracts. Some advice for the cooks with difficulties. If the cookies are too sticky, the butter and marshmallow were not cooked long enough. I prefer to cook these on the stove (without a double boiler) for more control. The trick to getting the red hots to stick is to work with another person to place them IMMEDIATELY. At my house, Holly Cookies are a "team event". While one person spoons out the cookies (and tries not to burn fingers :-) ) the other person follows right behind with the red hots -- good kid job!

Like the recipe I've used for more than 40 years, this recipe calls for almond extract as well as the vanilla, which I like. What's different about this recipe from mine is that it uses a tad more butter and marshmallows, which I thought might make this a little easier to mix with and coat the cornflakes but I learned the difference is negligible. Maybe I do it the hard way, but I neither microwave this nor use a double boiler. I just melt the marshmallows in a big non-stick Dutch oven over medium-low heat, which makes clean-up incredibly easy. Work fast and get yourself another set of hands to put the red hots on if you can because this sets up very quickly! Pretty and gooey and sweet, these have always been a favorite with both kids and adults alike. In fact, they are still one of my kids' favorites - and they're now 28 and 30 years old!

This is exactly how my mom always made them! Can't improve on perfection! I always laugh at people's reactions to green cornflakes, but yum. Messy to make though. We usually spray our hands with cooking spray and set them out on wax paper to reduce the stick factor.

I love this recipe--quick and easy--but found I needed to make some changes. The wreaths I made to the exact directions never hardened 100%. They hardened enough to serve them, but if you picked one up on a side, it would droop or break apart. I made some changes which produced a perfect wreath. I used an entire 10 oz. bag of marshmallows and increased the corn flakes to 4-1/2 cups. I lightly crushed the corn flakes by squeezing the bag they came in. The crushed flakes were much easier to form into the wreath shape, and I actually think they mimicked real greens more effectively. In an effort to reduce liquid (to make the wreaths harden better), I only used 1 tsp. of green food coloring. They weren't a bold green (as with 1 1-/2 tsp.), but they were certainly green enough. I also eliminated the almond flavoring. Instead of using waxed paper, I used ungreased parchment paper which worked much, much better. The wreaths didn't stick at all. I used a greased silicone spatula to quickly place blobs of mixture on the parchment. Then I dampened my fingers a bit, and shaped the blobs into wreaths, re-dampening my fingers if they began to stick. The water worked much better than buttered fingers and didn't seem to affect the firmness of the wreaths. The small amount of water dried in no time. With these changes, I give it stars!

I made 2 batches: the first in a saucepan and the second in the microwave. Surprisingly, the microwave batch was faster and made less of a mess. The marshmallows didn't melt uniformly in the saucepan whereas they puffed up and blended beautifully in the micowave. I doubled the vanilla extract and food coloring, and omitted the almond extract.

A true Christmas Classic! I am make these shaped like trees for my daughter's birthday treat at school every year. Just shape like a christmas tree and add sprinkles for lights or powdered sugar for snow. I make each one in a cupcake paper so she can easily pass them out. (I omit the almond extract when making for school in case of nut allergies.) Merry Christmas!

Haven't had these since I was a kid. I made these with Special K w/Berries. I removed the strawberries, broke them and added them after I formed the wreaths (using the end of a wooden spoon). I found the solution to the "sticky" storage problem. I dusted the wreaths with powdered sugar "snow" and lined the bottom of my container with it as well. Made them so much prettier - plus lots less sticky. The Special K and berries gave them an amazing flavor. Wish I had taken a photo. They were sooo pretty.

I haven't made these since I was in grade school!! I added a little more food coloring to make them pop and they looked great! I followed some of the advice in the reviews on here and they were helpful. Pam Pam Pam. These little devils are sticky. Pam on waxed paper and on my fingers between each wreath. When all was complete I had 12 good sized wreaths so I made 2 batches for my husband's Army unit.

Thank you for reminding me of one of my favorite holiday treats. I was so excited to be able to share this recipe with my 6-year old daughter this Christmas. I lined my baking sheets with wax paper and sprayed them with cooking spray and had no issues with them sticking. I used a 16oz bag of large marshmallows that and found that I did have to add about an extra cup of cornflakes to reach the correct texture. I handled the hot mixture and my daughter went behind me and added red M&M's instead of red hots - she doesn't like the red hots. We both loved them and look forward to making them again next year.

Tastes sooo good when done right. Can be a little time consuming when you're type A like me! I tried to make a larger batch and it seemed like I "over cooked" the cornflakes when I kept the pot even on low on the stove while I formed them on the wax paper. My suggestion.... make NO MORE than the recipe calls for. If you need more, make another batch!

Use your fingers but as someone said it’s so much easier to wet them to mold them. I dusted with a bit of powder sugar to give it snow but other than that followed directly (skittles though since the store didn’t have cinnamon hots) yummy!

4 minutes in the microwave for 1 stick of butter and 4 cups of mini-marshmallows is WAY too much. By the time the second 2-minute heating was done, the marshmallows had turned brown and caramelized. Stirring flavorings and food coloring into it was impossible, and within a few minutes, the whole mess hardened into concrete which, even after hours of soaking, will not come off my bowl and spoon. I wonder if the recipe writer has a microwave with lesser power, and if she tried it in a variety of microwaves to ensure the recipe worked with all of them, because they come in different wattages.

Great flavors but so sticky they didn't really set. I will compare ingredient amounts to other recipes, or try with more cornflakes next time. So good that I plan to make them in a pan for bars during the rest of the year without the green food coloring.

These turned out fairly well, and I agree with the tips - use gloves and get another person to help place the red dots. I used holiday M&Ms. The wreaths set up well enough that my guests could pick them up, though they were a little floppy even hours later. I will probably make these again. They are so festive!
I followed recipe as is. Do not try this recipe without a helper. Not a good recipe for humid Florida weather.
Loved it ! It was so yummy I just have no words!

I have very few positive childhood memories with my mother, but this recipe is one. She made a batch of these for my entire class every year that I was in elementary school -- 1980-85. I feel sure that my mom's recipe used an entire bag of marshmallows, and the wreaths were always perfectly firm and crisp, with glossy, green tops. I'm glad I came across this nostalgic recipe today and look forward to making a batch for the upcoming Christmas holiday.

This is a lot more fuss and faff than I ever did and I've been making them nearly 50yrs!! 6 Cups corn flakes ( Kelloggs are actually best-we've done taste tests) 25 reg marshmallows 6T butter 1t green food color 1t vanilla Melt the butter and marshmallows together in a pot on the stove medium low heat stirring frequently and keep pushing at the lumps of melting marshmallows till all melted Remove pan from heat and add vanilla and green food color mixing well to get uniform color distribution Quickly pour over cornflakes and stir to coat evenly. Working quickly, wear disposable gloves if you don't want green hands, drop a pile about the size of a soup spoon onto wax paper. Now you can shape them into a wreath BUT we gave that up several decades ago because they just go too fast. We also nixed the red hots because no one cared for them because it overpowered the flavor of the cookie. Now it's just the cookie part alone. IF you want to make the wreath shape and add red accents I suggest little pieces to red licorice or dried cranberry or red nonpareils. They do better packing them up if you let them sit on the wax paper for 5-6hrs , I fill the dining room table up with rows of green lumps, before layering them in a cookie tin or other tight lidded container between layers of waxed paper. We call ours Grinch cookies 🎄

Followed the recipe exactly, except could not add in all the cornflakes as there was not enough green goo. They were very hard to work. They were still too hot to work but already hardening. I've looked at other recipes since that call for more marshmallows and less heat. These were a disappointment!
I'm not sure what I've done wrong but they won't set and are so soft that can hardly pick them up. Very disappointed cos they look adorable but I can't let my kids bring them to school.
